//: Metadata for the patch-package patches in this directory — one key per patched npm package. Consumed by the orphaned-patch guard (packages/dev-tools/patch-reconcile/check-patches.mjs, run as `npm run lint:patches`) and the renovate-patch-reconcile workflow. Every patches/<pkg>+<version>.patch MUST have an entry here with a matching patchedVersion. When a patch is removed, delete its entry. See patches/README.md.

@zenfs/core.reason: #2146: VCache.ref coalesced DIFFERENT paths onto one vnode when their inodes shared an ino (poisoned indexes carry many ino-0 entries) — the shared inode object cross-stamps size/mode between unrelated files. The patch refuses cross-path coalescing unless the inodes are a genuine hardlink: ino must be nonzero, format bits must match, AND nlink must be > 1 on both sides (#2034). A duplicated real ino with nlink 1 is a poisoned index, not a link — and because every vnode also owns its sparse data cache, two colliding paths open at once returned each other's bytes (8 parallel preview fetches all served the entry file; sequential reads evicted the vnode between calls and were correct). 2.7.3 (zen-fs/core#314) only emits a non-fatal error when nlink === paths.size on a new path; it still returns the shared vnode, so the refuse-to-coalesce hunk stays. (The patch also used to carry an Index._alloc() hunk for zen-fs/core#312 — the Math.max spread of 2x entryCount arguments that threw RangeError('Maximum call stack size exceeded') on every createFile/mkdir once the OPFS index grew large. That fix shipped upstream in 2.6.5, which now reduces instead of spreading and memoizes the last id, so the hunk is gone; tests/fs/zenfs-alloc-overflow-upstream.test.ts pins the upstream behavior.) ALSO (zen-fs/core#318 / slicc#3101): core 2.7.3 acquires a whole-tree payload semaphore and dom 1.2.14 initializes it; SLICC configures the released limiter to 16, so the patch no longer maintains a second concurrency cap. The remaining crossCopy delta shares the first read/stat/readdir failure across the preload tree, checks it after a semaphore handoff before allocating or reading, awaits all descendants so active reads drain, and preserves the first error. Browser repro: packages/webapp/tests/e2e/zenfs-preload/.
@zenfs/core.removeWhen: Keep the VCache hunk until @zenfs/core refuses to share a vnode across paths for non-hardlink inodes — 2.7.3's zen-fs/core#314 only logs the mismatch. (The patch also used to rewrite `globalThis.__zenfs__` into an own-property copy so a probe could enumerate it; upstream declined that in https://github.com/zen-fs/core/issues/310 — the global is deliberately minimal — so that hunk is gone and consumers must probe by existence plus the `_version` export instead.) Remove the preload error-path hunk once Async.crossCopy shares the first traversal failure, starts no queued backend work after failure, and waits for issued work before ready() rejects. The concurrency limiter itself is already upstream in core 2.7.3 + dom 1.2.14 and must not be reintroduced here.
@zenfs/core.verify: npm run test -w @slicc/webapp -- zenfs-ino-collision-patch virtual-fs-concurrent-read zenfs-alloc-overflow-upstream zenfs-preload-concurrency

@zenfs/dom.reason: #2146 leftover: 1.2.14 (zen-fs/dom#43) allocates unique ino/data pairs in WebAccessFS.stat's ENOENT recovery and _loadMetadata's reality branch, so the minting hunks are gone; tests/fs/zenfs-ino-collision-patch.test.ts pins the upstream _alloc(). Those allocations still omit nlink, and ZenFS's Inode constructor warns on every ino!=0/nlink==0 inode while kerium retains every log entry — leaving nlink unset flooded the in-memory log on every inode materialization until its backing Set hit V8's 2^24 cap and every FS op threw 'Set maximum size exceeded' (2026-08-18 VFS-offline incident). The remaining hunk sets nlink: 1 at both sites. ALSO (#2157): 1.2.14 (zen-fs/dom#45) now materializes zero-byte files through WebAccessFS._create and IndexFS.createFile rolls its index insert back if creation fails, so the redundant createFile override is gone. The patch still makes remove tolerate an already-absent OPFS entry — IndexFS has already validated existence against the authoritative index, so an entry it knows but OPFS does not (a legacy file or a sidecar entry whose bytes vanished) would otherwise be undeletable forever. (The patch also used to carry a keepExistingData hunk in write; that fix shipped upstream in 1.2.11 via WebAccessFS.touch.) ALSO (zen-fs/dom#46): a concurrent overwrite invalidates the File returned by getFile(), so arrayBuffer() throws NotReadableError even for a six-byte file. Reacquire the snapshot for at most three attempts; other errors and persistent failures still propagate. The real-Chromium repro controls the overwrite interleaving without injecting an exception: packages/webapp/tests/e2e/zenfs-opfs-read-race/.
@zenfs/dom.removeWhen: Split by hunk. The nlink: 1 hunks can drop once WebAccess sets nlink at both minting sites (1.2.14 still omits it; Inode still warns on ino!=0/nlink==0). The zero-byte create side is upstream in 1.2.14 via WebAccessFS._create. The remove hunk can drop once WebAccessFS.remove tolerates an OPFS entry the index knows but the store does not (1.2.14 still rethrows ENOENT). Remove the snapshot-read hunk once zen-fs/dom#46 ships bounded NotReadableError retries with freshly acquired File snapshots.
@zenfs/dom.verify: npm run test -w @slicc/webapp -- zenfs-dom-truncate-upstream zero-byte-file-delete zenfs-ino-collision-patch zenfs-opfs-read-retry

isomorphic-git.reason: #2735: `readObjectPacked`'s packfile integrity check is guarded by a `p._checksumVerified` boolean that is only set AFTER its `await`, so every reader that arrives while the first SHA-1 is in flight starts its own hash of the WHOLE pack — `_walk` fans object reads out with `Promise.all`, so the 92 MB slicc pack was hashed 8-9 times per command (5,195 ms in `digest` on a hostfs mount vs 603 ms for one hash), each duplicate also copying the input for WebCrypto. The patch extracts the check into `verifyPackfileIntegrity()` and memoizes it as a promise on the cached pack index (`p._verification`), so N concurrent readers verify exactly once. The memo records whether it INCLUDED the deep hash (`p._deepVerified`), so a caller that turns verification back on mid-shell is not served the promise of the run that skipped it. #2710: the deep (full payload) SHA-1 has no upstream switch, and it is not something canonical git does on an object read (it verifies packs on `fsck` / `index-pack`); the patch skips it when the caller's cache object carries `skipDeepPackVerification`, which SLICC sets by default for its VFS/hostfs-backed repos (`packages/webapp/src/git/git-cache.ts`, `$SLICC_GIT_VERIFY_PACKS=1` opts back in). The O(1) trailer check always runs. The patch also stamps a monotonic `_lastUsedAt` on each pack index it serves a read from, which is what lets SLICC's long-lived cache evict the least recently used pack BUFFERS instead of holding every pack it ever touched. Only `index.js` (the ESM entry) is patched: the browser build and vitest both alias `isomorphic-git` to it on purpose because the CJS entry imports Node crypto (tests/git/isomorphic-git-esm.test.ts).
isomorphic-git.removeWhen: Remove the memoization hunk once isomorphic-git verifies a packfile once per pack rather than once per concurrent reader, and the skip hunk once it exposes an option to skip the deep payload verification on read.

kerium.reason: kerium's log() retains EVERY entry in a module-global List (a plain Set underneath) with no cap or rotation — even entries below the output threshold that are never printed (default minLevel is ALERT). A long-lived kernel worker under log pressure (e.g. ZenFS's per-inode nlink warning) eventually hits V8's 2^24-element Set cap, after which entries.add throws RangeError('Set maximum size exceeded') into every logging caller — every ZenFS op failed and the VFS went offline (2026-08-18 incident). The patch evicts the oldest entry beyond a 10,000-entry ring so the backlog stays bounded.
kerium.removeWhen: Remove once kerium bounds its log backlog upstream (ring buffer or opt-in retention).

just-bash.reason: curl formats the response for stdout (`N(...)` → latin1 decode of the WHOLE body via `Buffer.from(body).toString('binary')`) BEFORE checking `-o`/`-O`, then discards the string. In the browser the `buffer` polyfill's latin1Slice builds that string one `+=` per byte, so every downloaded byte costs a ~32-byte V8 cons-string node: a 250 MB `curl -o` needed ~8 GB of V8 heap and crashed the leader tab (renderer OOM → Inspector.targetCrashed). The patch skips the stdout formatting when the body is going to a file (unless `-v`, which still prints it), so `curl -o` costs the body bytes, not a string copy of them. Multipart file fields use the optional readFileBytes API (binary read fallback); headers and inline fields are encoded as UTF-8 bytes before composing the latin1 body, preserving binary uploads alongside Unicode text.
just-bash.removeWhen: Remove once just-bash's curl only formats the body for stdout when it will be printed (or streams `-o` output to the fs). The multipart form builder must also read raw file bytes and encode text fields separately.
